STEP 1 - Scene: This looks like a plate of raw or lightly prepared cut squash/pumpkin (orange flesh, peeled wedges and cubes), not a full cooked meal. It is photographed from above at a steep angle, with the plate tilted toward the camera.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white plate is an oval/triangular-ish serving plate about 26 cm long at its longest undistorted width. Treating it as a dinner-plate-sized vessel with an effective diameter of about 24 cm gives area ≈ 3.14 × 12² ≈ 452 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: One food: orange cut squash/pumpkin pieces (roughly 8–10 wedges and chunks, each about 4–5 cm long and 2–3 cm thick).

STEP 4 - Area: The pieces cover roughly 25% of the plate area (about 113 cm²).

STEP 5 - Volume: 113 cm² × ~2 cm average pile height ≈ 226 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: 226 ml × 0.6 g/ml (cut vegetable pieces) ≈ 135 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Raw winter squash/pumpkin is about 26–40 kcal per 100 g; using ~30 kcal/100 g gives 135 g × 0.30 ≈ 40 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Roughly 135 g of cut squash on a large plate is plausible for a small portion. The estimate is an approximation from a single photo, and the food's cooking state is uncertain (if cooked without oil, energy would be similar; if roasted in oil, it would be higher).
